Ostroleka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ostrołęka, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Ostrołęka developed in the early 19th century; population reached 57.3% (4,564) by 1897, declining to 36.6% (3,352) by 1921. Germans expelled Jews in October 1939; many reached Soviet territory, while others were exterminated in the Vilnius and Słonim ghettos. This cemetery, likely established around 1822 alongside synagogue supervision funding, served Ostrołęka and surrounding villages including Andrzejewo, Czarnów, Czerwin, Kaczyna, and Wólka Brzezińska; walled and partially forested pre-war grounds covered about 3.6 hectares. Postwar development gradually built over the site: a housing estate, Korczaka Street cut through the grounds, and a school with childcare facilities occupied the southern portion. A 1989 commemorative plaque and 1991 tombstone-fragment monument followed local initiative; a 2004 restitution application by the Union of Jewish Religious Communities in Poland was unsuccessful. 2008-2009 Korczaka Street reconstruction disturbed graves, with the dug-up bones reburied near the Poznańska Street monument in 2010.
